findings.declaration: E4_ne_zero / E6_ne_zero / delta_ne_zero (missing simp lemma for coefficients of laurentOfInt)
findings.excerpt:
simp only [laurentOfInt_apply, HahnSeries.ofPowerSeries_apply_coeff, PowerSeries.coeff_map,
    HahnSeries.coeff_zero] at h1
findings.problem: The three non-vanishing proofs repeat the same `simp only` list. They unfold `laurentOfInt_apply` and then push the coefficient through `ofPowerSeries_apply_coeff` and `coeff_map`. They then still need a manual `rw` with `coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff_apply` and `constantCoeff_*`. The interface has no canonical simp lemma for the coefficient of `laurentOfInt K f` at a natural-number index. `laurentOfInt_apply` is not simp, and unfolding it exposes `ofPowerSeries` and `map`. Each caller therefore rebuilds the normal form by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Next to `laurentOfInt`, add a lemma such as `(laurentOfInt K f).coeff (n : ℤ) = Int.cast (PowerSeries.coeff n f)` for `n : ℕ`, marked @[simp], with its proof being the `simp only` call above. Optionally add a `coeff_zero`/`coeff_succ_X_mul` variant. Each of the three `_ne_zero` proofs can then be roughly `intro h; simpa using congrArg (fun x => x.coeff (n : ℤ)) h`.
findings.benefit: The three proofs shrink and share one normal form. Later users of `laurentOfInt` get coefficient extraction through `simp` instead of copying the four-lemma `simp only` list.

evidence.excerpt:
theorem laurentOfInt_apply (K : Type*) [CommRing K] (f : PowerSeries ℤ) :
    laurentOfInt K f = HahnSeries.ofPowerSeries ℤ K (f.map (Int.castRingHom K)) := rfl

findings.excerpt: theorem intSeriesC_eq_laurentOfInt (p : PowerSeries ℤ) : intSeriesC K p = laurentOfInt K p := rfl
findings.problem: `intSeriesC K` and `laurentOfInt K` are two definitionally equal presentations of one map. Only `laurentOfInt` is a RingHom, so `map_mul`, `map_pow` and `map_sub` apply to it as simp lemmas. The bridge lemma has no simp attribute and is applied only by `rw`. `thetaL_mul_delta` has to say `rw [intSeriesC_eq_laurentOfInt, intSeriesC_eq_laurentOfInt, map_mul (laurentOfInt K) (eisenstein4 ^ 2), map_pow] at h` with the arguments spelled out. The main theorem closes the same gap with a bare `rfl`. The sibling file `..._eq_one_of_mem_ssPlaces` declares the identical lemma again and also uses it only by `rw`.
findings.proposed_change: Move this lemma to the definition of `intSeriesC` (Def_ModularCurve_X1), or `laurentOfInt`, and mark it @[simp]. It rewrites toward the RingHom form and cannot cycle, since there is no reverse rule. The `rw` chain in `thetaL_mul_delta` could then become `simpa [← map_pow, ← map_mul] using h`, or just `simpa using h` once the matching map_mul/map_pow normal form is available. Delete the duplicate copies in the `Sol` files.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical normal form (`laurentOfInt`) for integer-coefficient Laurent series. Rewrites and ring-hom simp lemmas then fire automatically. Users no longer repeat the lemma per file or fall back on `rfl` to cross the boundary.

evidence.excerpt:
def intSeriesC (p : PowerSeries ℤ) : LaurentSeries K :=
  HahnSeries.ofPowerSeries ℤ K (p.map (Int.castRingHom K))
theorem intSeriesC_eq_laurentOfInt (p : PowerSeries ℤ) : intSeriesC K p = laurentOfInt K p := rfl

findings.declaration: ord_jGeomGen_sub (ite-valued statement) and its uses in `solution`
findings.excerpt: = if x.evalAt (jGeomGen K N) = c then (placeRamificationJ N x : ℤ) else 0
findings.problem: The statement is a single `if … then … else` that needs `[DecidableEq K]`. In `solution` every use has to be split by hand into the three evalAt cases. Each case ends with a manual `rw [if_pos he0] at h0` or `rw [if_neg he1] at h1`, six times in total. These rewrites are exactly what `simp` would do given hypotheses `he0 : v.evalAt J = 0` and so on. As an ite lemma it is not a usable simp rule without a decidability instance, and the condition must match syntactically. The file also adds `[DecidableEq K]` to the section only for this lemma.
findings.proposed_change: State two decidability-free lemmas, `ord_jGeomGen_sub_of_evalAt_eq (h : x.evalAt (jGeomGen K N) = c) : ord (…) = placeRamificationJ N x` and `ord_jGeomGen_sub_of_evalAt_ne (h : … ≠ c) : ord (…) = 0`. Make them simp lemmas with their side conditions as hypotheses, or keep the ite lemma as a corollary. The case branches of `solution` can then call them directly and skip the `if_pos`/`if_neg` rewrites. The `DecidableEq K` variable can be dropped.
findings.benefit: The case analysis no longer needs `rw [if_pos/if_neg] at` plumbing. The lemma needs no decidability assumption. It can be used by `simp` once the evalAt hypotheses are in context.
